```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false


library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(knitr)
library(jsonlite)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +   # 9pt fits well at 3.6in column width
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )
)

get_latest_acs5_year <- function() {
  api_catalog <- fromJSON("https://api.census.gov/data.json")$dataset
  tibble(
    year = as.numeric(api_catalog$c_vintage),
    dataset = map_chr(api_catalog$c_dataset, paste, collapse = "-")
  ) |> 
    filter(dataset == "acs-acs5") |> 
    pull(year) |> 
    max(na.rm = TRUE)
}

current_acs_year <- get_latest_acs5_year()

```

```{r}
#| label: generate-reports
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

# Define your test towns
towns <- c("Auburn", "Barre", "Berlin", "Blackstone", "Boylston", "Brookfield", "Charlton",
  "Douglas", "Dudley", "East Brookfield", "Grafton", "Hardwick", "Holden", "Hopedale",
  "Leicester", "Mendon", "Millbury", "Millville", "New Braintree", "North Brookfield",
  "Northborough", "Northbridge", "Oakham", "Oxford", "Paxton", "Princeton", "Rutland",
  "Shrewsbury", "Southbridge", "Spencer", "Sturbridge", "Sutton", "Upton", "Uxbridge",
  "Warren", "Webster", "West Boylston", "West Brookfield", "Westborough", "Worcester") 

# 1. Expand the template to fill in the {{town_name}} for each town
src <- lapply(towns, function(current_town) {
  knitr::knit_expand("_town_template.qmd", town_name = current_town)
})

# 2. Knit the expanded text so it properly generates and saves the plots
res <- knitr::knit_child(text = unlist(src), quiet = TRUE)

# 3. 'cat' prints the raw markdown (and plot links) directly into the final document
cat(res, sep = '\n')
```
